title: Finite affine lifting and eventual vanishing for annihilator quotients
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\iota:\mathcal I\hookrightarrow\mathcal O_X$ a monomorphism of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with $\mathcal I$ quasi-coherent and of finite type [pqf-def-coherent]. Put $P_n=\mathcal I^n$ with inclusion $j_n:P_n\hookrightarrow\mathcal O_X$ and $P_0=\mathcal O_X$, using the recursive ideal powers of [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-module-product-stalk]. Assume $X$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let $\mathcal F$ be quasi-coherent. Let $U\subseteq X$ be open with $x\in U$ if and only if $\iota_x$ is surjective. Fix sections $1_n\in P_n(U)$ with $j_n(1_n)=1$ and maps $r_{nm}:P_m\to P_n$ for $n\le m$ with $j_n r_{nm}=j_m$. For an $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ and any open $W$, say a section $s\in\mathcal F(W)$ is annihilated by $P_n$ if for every open $W\prime\subseteq W$ and every $b\in P_n(W\prime)$, the product $j_n(b)s|_{W\prime}$ is zero. Fix quasi-coherent $A_n$, monomorphisms $a_n:A_n\to\mathcal F$ whose sectionwise images are exactly these annihilators, and assume every $\pi_n(W):\mathcal F(W)\to Q_n(W)$ is bijective for $W\subseteq U$, where $Q_n=\operatorname{coker}(a_n)$ and $\pi_n$ is the cokernel projection [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Fix $q_{nm}:Q_n\to Q_m$ with $q_{nm}\pi_n=\pi_m$ for $n\le m$. Then (i) if $\varphi:P_n\to Q_n$ has $\varphi_U(1_n)=0$, some $m\ge n$ satisfies $q_{nm}\varphi r_{nm}=0$; (ii) every $s\in\mathcal F(U)$ has $\pi_{n,U}(s)=\varphi_U(1_n)$ for some $n$ and $\varphi:P_n\to Q_n$. No colimit or diagram is part of this conclusion.

proof.text: On an affine open write the modules as M and J, with J finitely generated. The annihilator condition identifies A_n with the sheaf of M_n={x:J^n x=0}, and the cokernel with the sheaf of M/M_n. For a map whose evaluation vanishes, the generator and monomial calculation of 01PM kills the map on a higher power; the quotient transition preserves zero. A finite affine cover and the maximum exponent give assertion (i).

source.place: Lemma 01PQ (lemma-sections-over-quasi-compact-open), proof; Lemma 01PM (lemma-sections-over-quasi-compact-open-in-affine), proof. Source text read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01PQ and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01PM.

proof.text: Represent a section by x_i/f_i^k on the finitely many principal opens of an affine complement. Clear denominators on overlaps so f_j^k x_i=f_i^k x_j. Let K be the module annihilated by all f_i^k. At sufficiently large monomial degree d, select an exponent at least k and send the monomial to the product with that exponent lowered by k, times x_i, modulo K. Multiplication by any f_j^k turns a relation among monomials into the original relation times x_j. Hence the map is well defined. Enlarge d so K is contained in M_d and compose to M/M_d. It evaluates to the given section.

source.place: Lemma 01PQ (lemma-sections-over-quasi-compact-open), proof; Lemma 01PM (lemma-sections-over-quasi-compact-open-in-affine), proof. Source text read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01PQ and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01PM.

proof.text: Choose a finite affine cover with quasi-compact overlaps. The previous affine construction gives local lifts. Differences of lifts on an overlap have zero evaluation after passage to a common degree, so assertion (i) on a finite affine overlap cover makes them equal at a later degree. Take the maximum over all covers and overlaps, and glue the resulting maps. Sheaf uniqueness and bijectivity of the quotient projection on U identify the evaluation with the desired section.
